scope: Narrow source-only review of v8 private transport error retention and launcher/scenario delta against frozen v7. No tests/apps/browser/Docker and no private runtime files read.

findings.result: Both exact known CDP socket and Playwright socketerror hooks synchronously call private record before the existing public projection. The module writes and fsyncs the JSON-escaped original string before returning only ordinal, UTF8 byte count, SHA256 and retainedPrivately flag.

Fresh canonical owned private parent; exclusive no-follow append ordinary single-link0600 file. 2048-byte per-error,32 rows,128KiB total refusal; raw arbitrary strings remain private JSONL. Neither record return nor snapshot exports raw error text, private path, URL or headers.

Validation/cap/write/sync errors set a sticky capture failure and throw fixed static errors; guarded CDP and Playwright callbacks retain observer failure rather than throwing out of event delivery. Launcher onFailure sets workflow failure. Close validates identity/size/parent and fsync/close acknowledgement. The bounded independent cleanup phase records failed capture and prevents overall pass; later cleanup phases remain reachable.

Existing read gate budget, Create/Restart count and terminal close/error assertions are unchanged; no fallback, replay or admission changes. Actual v7 unknown error remains unavailable; this prospective correction does not recover original text.

limitations: Synchronous filesystem writes/fsync/close cannot be preempted by JS timer; independent outer watchdog remains required for a hard process bound.
Close-phase snapshot success concerns private capture only, not socket/terminal/application success.
Incoming strings originate in observer APIs; capture validates UTF8 byte length after conversion and does not claim arbitrary upstream allocation bounds.
No new controls executed or independent count audit in this source review; parent-reported original8pass2fail/fixed10pass remain separate from this review.
Raw file must remain excluded from publication. Unknown strings can contain sensitive data despite deliberately limited collection.
